meta.title: Flappyboard — a split-flap message board for your television
meta.description: Type on your phone and the flaps turn on the TV in the other room. 24 × 6 flaps, 144 in all, running in the television's own browser.

lede.title: A split-flap message board that runs on the television you already own.
lede.body: Point the TV's browser at one address and it becomes a board. After that anyone in the house can write to it from their phone — or ask the LLM a question and let it set the answer in flaps.
lede.screensaver: Is it just a screensaver? No. A screensaver has nothing to say. This holds whatever the last person put there, in the room they put it, until somebody changes it.

say.label: Type here — the board above follows
say.note: A–Z, 0–9 and punctuation. The drums are Latin.

hint.dropped: A flap can show A–Z, 0–9 and punctuation. Anything else was left off — the real board does the same.
hint.nothing: Nothing in that line has a flap, so the board is holding what it last showed. The drums are Latin: a real split-flap shows the same letters everywhere it is sold.
hint.full: That is more than the board holds. The rest fell off the bottom.

tv.label: On your TV's browser, go to
tv.body: That is the setup, all of it. A television with a browser opens the address and shows a six-character code; the phone that types the code owns the board. Nothing to install, nothing to plug in, no box on the shelf.

specs.title: Specifications
specs.caption: What the board is and what it runs on

characters.label: Character set
characters.value: 57 flaps per drum: the blank, A–Z, 0–9 and 20 marks of punctuation

pigments.label: Pigments
pigments.value: 6 colours, plus lit white and unlit — measured off a real unit

rate.label: Flap rate
rate.value: 14 a second — one flap every 72 ms

travel.label: Longest travel
travel.value: 4.2 s, one end of the drum to the other

written.label: Written from
written.value: Any phone in the house, over a live socket

agent.label: Or written by
agent.value: The LLM, when you ask it a question instead of typing an answer

runs.label: Runs on
runs.value: Any television with a browser — Chromium 56 and up, so a 2017 panel is fine

pairing.label: Pairing
pairing.value: A six-character code on the screen, or scan the QR beside it

sound.label: Sound
sound.value: The clatter, out of the television — not out of your phone

footer.note: A message board that lives in the room, not in a feed.
